task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of September 8, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style reported feature about Pellwren Instruments and the small calibration business serving growers who rely on environmental sensors.

facts.text: An August 2026 bench note records technician Ceri Alven comparing a greenhouse temperature sensor with the workshop's reference instrument.
Pellwren Instruments employs Alven and owner Neri Warden, serving growers and small food-storage businesses.
Its last annual ledger records 340 calibration jobs: 210 temperature, 80 humidity and 50 pressure instruments.
Those are instrument jobs, not 340 different farms or a count of defective devices.

The supplied bench example shows a sensor reading 20.1 degrees Celsius against a 20-degree reference; that indicated 0.1-degree difference is within the customer's stated 0.2-degree tolerance at that point.
The certificate covers specified checks from 10 to 30 degrees Celsius, not every temperature or field condition; the packet provides no uncertainty analysis.
Calibration compares readings with a reference; it does not by itself prove a sensor was installed in a representative place in a greenhouse.
Warden says a sensor near a door can correctly measure that location while giving a poor picture of conditions around plants farther inside.
Warden said, "A correct number can still be answering the wrong question if the sensor is in the wrong place."
The workshop's standard bench check starts at $75 per instrument, with travel, parts and unusual ranges priced separately.
Some older units cannot be adjusted because their manufacturers no longer supply the necessary parts or software support.
Grower Omi Velden sends several sensors together during quieter production periods to reduce repeated travel charges.
Velden keeps a spare sensor available because the usual workshop turnaround is ten working days.
Velden said, "The instrument is small. Working without its reading for two weeks is not a small decision."
The workshop records whether a device was checked, adjusted or returned without adjustment, rather than calling every job a repair.
The owner reports increasing inquiries but has not supplied a consistent historical series proving the whole regional market is growing.
The record contains no measured crop-yield or water-saving benefit attributable to this particular sensor service.
The business schedules field visits around both growers' access windows and the time needed to maintain its own reference equipment.
Pellwren operates from a converted veterinary supply office, with a separate temperature-controlled bench room.
The owner has considered hiring a third worker but has not offered a job or secured a new long-term customer contract.

forbidden_additions: Every calibration is a repair or a passing bench check proves ideal field placement
Verified crop gains, regional market growth or a third employee already hired
